advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tie the envelope-difference guard to actual behavior: assert `_normalize` drops exactly the enumerated fields (e.g. compare a raw captured payload against its normalized form) instead of grepping the `ENVELOPE_DIFFERENCES` prose tuple for substrings.
evidence: `joined = " ".join(ENVELOPE_DIFFERENCES).lower()` then `for token in (...): assert token in joined` (tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py:590-601)

`ENVELOPE_DIFFERENCES` is a test-local prose tuple (tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py:398-415); a repo-wide search finds it referenced only at its definition, in `_normalize`'s docstring, and in this test — no production code and no parser/validator consumes it (search_files ENVELOPE_DIFFERENCES: lines 398, 420, 590 only)

`_normalize` (tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py:418-451) enumerates normalized-away fields in code (`modelId`/`inferenceConfig.maxTokens`/`temperature`/`toolConfig`/etc.) and does NOT read `ENVELOPE_DIFFERENCES`, so the list and the behavior can drift apart while the test stays green

Refactoring/regression-blindness: if `_normalize` starts normalizing a NEW field away (the regression the docstring names), this test cannot detect it; conversely a behavior-preserving reword of the prose (e.g. changing the literal `converse_stream` spelling) turns it RED with no observable-behavior change
advisory.finding: `test_the_enumerated_envelope_differences_are_the_only_ones_normalized` is a change-detector on prose: it greps the test-local `ENVELOPE_DIFFERENCES` string tuple for hard-coded substrings, but that tuple is documentation only — the `_normalize` function that actually decides which fields are normalized away never references it. The test therefore verifies the author's wording, not the normalizer's behavior, and has no regression coverage of the contract its own docstring claims ('name every field the comparison normalizes away, so a future divergence cannot hide').
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the prose-substring loop with an assertion over `_normalize`'s behavior — e.g. feed a synthetic Bedrock and Anthropic payload carrying each enumerated envelope field and assert those keys are absent from the normalized dict while the semantic fields survive, so the test breaks when the normalizer's field set changes rather than when the documentation wording changes.

coaching.coaching: Delete the change-detector / tautological test the prose change-detector on ENVELOPE_DIFFERENCES strings; do not re-pin it to the new source text — a test that only mirrors the implementation asserts nothing.
coaching.subject: the prose change-detector on ENVELOPE_DIFFERENCES strings
